samples.text:
The bar chart shows how many minutes men and women in five countries spent for unpaid housework each day.

In all five countries women spent more time than men. The biggest difference is in Country X, where women did housework for 290 minutes but men only did 45 minutes. In Country V, women spent 240 minutes and men spent 80 minutes, so women spent three times more than men.

In Country W and Country Z, men did more housework than in the other countries. Men in Country Z spent 170 minutes, which was the highest for men, and women spent 245 minutes. In Country W, the figures was 150 minutes for men and 225 minutes for women, so the difference was not very big.

Country Y had the smallest gap between men and women. Women spent 170 minutes, it was the lowest figure for women, and men spent 110 minutes.

Overall, women do much more unpaid housework than men in every countries, but the difference between men and women is not same in each country.
samples.why: Figures accurate with some comparison · overview present but only at the end · mechanical linking · limited vocabulary · preposition, agreement, tense and punctuation errors that do not impede meaning.

samples.text:
The chart compares the average amount of time that men and women in five countries spent each day on unpaid household work.

Overall, women spent more time on household tasks than men in every country, although the size of the gap varied considerably. It was widest in Country X and narrowest in Country Y.

The difference was most pronounced in Country X, where women did 290 minutes of unpaid work per day, the highest figure on the chart, while men contributed only 45 minutes, the lowest. A similar, though less extreme, pattern was found in Country V, with women spending 240 minutes on housework, three times as much as men (80 minutes).

In the remaining three countries, men took a greater share of household work. Men in Country Z spent 170 minutes a day on these tasks, more than in any other country, compared to 245 minutes for women. The figures for Country W was similar, at 150 and 225 minutes respectively, a gap of 75 minutes in both cases. In Country Y, women spent 170 minutes a day on housework, the least of all the countries, and men 110 minutes, leaving a difference of just 60 minutes.
samples.why: Clear overview of the gender gap and its variation · key features highlighted with accurate comparisons · logical grouping · good range of linkers and vocabulary · one minor agreement slip.

samples.text:
The bar chart compares the average daily time spent on unpaid domestic work by men and women in five countries.

Women consistently undertook more unpaid household work than men, but the extent of the imbalance differed markedly between countries. It was greatest in Country X and smallest in Country Y, while men's contribution was highest in Countries Z and W.

In Country X, women devoted 290 minutes a day to domestic tasks, almost five hours and the highest figure shown, whereas men spent just 45 minutes, meaning that women did more than six times as much. Country V displayed a similar, if less pronounced, imbalance: women's 240 minutes were exactly three times the 80 minutes recorded for men.

The division of labour was considerably more even elsewhere. Men in Country Z spent 170 minutes on household work, the most for any male group, and those in Country W 150 minutes; women in these countries spent 245 and 225 minutes respectively, a gap of 75 minutes in each case. Country Y had the narrowest difference, just 60 minutes, as women there spent the least time of any female group (170 minutes) and men 110 minutes.
samples.why: Key features skilfully selected with accurate derived ratios · clear overview · logical grouping from largest to smallest gap · cohesion managed well · precise vocabulary · wide range of structures, error-free.
